title: Central Asia

cards.b: Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan) has energy, uranium, minerals and a position between Russia, China, Iran and Afghanistan. India has deep history here but no land access, because Pakistan and Afghanistan lie in between. UPSC asks about connectivity, SCO and rivalry with China.

• 1991-92: ties with the five new republics after the USSR's breakup.
  • 2012: Connect Central Asia policy (a four-C framework: commerce, connectivity, consular, community).
  • July 2015: Modi visited all five in one tour.
  • 2017: India became a full member of the SCO.
  • 2019: first India-Central Asia Dialogue (Samarkand).
  • January 2022: first India-Central Asia Summit (virtual); a summit mechanism was institutionalised.

The International North-South Transport Corridor (2000; India, Iran, Russia) links Mumbai to Bandar Abbas and Russia via the Caspian. Chabahar (Iran) gives a sea route bypassing Pakistan: a 2016 trilateral agreement with Iran and Afghanistan, and a 10-year operating contract (2024). India also joined the Ashgabat Agreement (2018). Chabahar's future depends on US sanctions waivers and Iran's politics; its status in 2026 has been uncertain, so check.

The TAPI pipeline (Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India, about 1,800 km) has been stuck for years because of security and politics. India buys uranium from Kazakhstan (Kazatomprom contracts) for its nuclear plants. India has stakes in Kazakhstan's oil field Satpayev (ONGC Videsh) and seeks rare earths and critical minerals.

Joint military exercises: Khanjar (Kyrgyzstan), Dustlik (Uzbekistan), Prabal and Kazind. Tajikistan's Ayni airbase (with India's help) and the Farkhor hospital base show strategic interest. India uses the SCO-RATS (Tashkent) for counter-terrorism. After the Taliban takeover of Kabul in 2021, Central Asian states and India share worry over extremism, and India's Delhi Regional Security Dialogue on Afghanistan (2018, 2021) included them.

• No direct access: Pakistan blocks transit; Afghanistan is unstable.
  • China's footprint: Belt and Road, pipelines, investment, and the China-Central Asia mechanism.
  • Russia remains the security patron (CSTO).
  • Trade is small, below 2 billion US dollars a year; India's market is far.
  • India declined to join BRI and the SCO's BRI statements.

Bollywood, Hindi films, yoga and medicine are popular. India's tools: ITEC training, e-networks, an IT centre in each republic, lines of credit, and the proposed India-Central Asia Development Group and a Rare Earth Forum. The people-to-people links also include education: many Central Asian students study in India.

Policy summary: a multi-alignment approach, using the SCO, INSTC and Chabahar, plus bilateral energy and defence ties. It is part of India's 'Extended Neighbourhood' idea and balances against China without confrontation. Compare with the Look East / Act East policy, which is the east-facing equivalent. The India-Central Asia summit was meant to be held regularly.
